content.title: About
content.content: Beef Stroganoff with noodles is a classic Russian dish featuring tender strips of beef simmered in a creamy mushroom sauce and served over boiled noodles. The combination of a rich sauce and hearty noodles makes it a favorite both at home and in restaurants.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The dish is named after Russian Count Stroganov, though the original recipe differs greatly from modern versions.
Traditional sauce is made with sour cream, tomato paste, and mushrooms, but regional variations add wine, mustard, or soy sauce.
Noodles served with Stroganoff are often egg noodles, but any pasta type—spaghetti, fettuccine, or rice noodles—can be used.
The dish became popular in the United States in the early 20th century, where it is commonly called “Stroganoff” and served with pasta.
A vegetarian version replaces beef with mushrooms while preserving the creamy flavor.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Beef provides high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Beef is a good source of heme iron, which is more readily absorbed than plant‑based iron.

items.title: Calcium and vitamin D from sour cream
items.content: The creamy sauce adds calcium and vitamin D, supporting bone health.

items.title: Mushrooms supply B‑vitamins
items.content: Mushrooms contribute vitamins B2, B3, and B5, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Carbohydrates from noodles provide energy
items.content: Boiled noodles deliver quick‑release carbs to maintain energy levels.

items.title: High in saturated fat
items.content: Cream and beef can raise cholesterol levels if consumed frequently.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: The sauce often contains salt; people with hypertension should monitor intake.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Sour cream may trigger reactions in those with lactose intolerance or milk allergy.

items.title: Digestive heaviness of red meat
items.content: Some individuals may experience discomfort due to the richness of beef.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the Stroganoff hot, ladling the sauce over the beef and noodles. Garnish with fresh parsley or dill and a pinch of black pepper. For a healthier twist, use whole‑grain pasta to increase fiber content.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. For longer storage, freeze in portion‑size bags for up to 2 months. Reheat gently, bringing the sauce back to a gentle boil to prevent separation.
